title: Binary Subarrays With Sum
statement: The list contains only 0s and 1s. Return how many non-empty contiguous subarrays sum to exactly goal.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(27)
    return [[r.randint(0, 1) for _ in range(100000)], 1000]

hints.1_question: A subarray sum is a difference of two prefix sums. For each position, how many earlier prefixes equal (current - goal)?
hints.2_nudge: Keep a count map of prefix sums seen so far, starting with {0: 1} for the empty prefix.
hints.3_big_hint: total += x; count += seen.get(total - goal, 0); seen[total] += 1.

known_bugs.name: forgets the empty prefix
known_bugs.followup: How do you count a subarray that starts at index 0? Which prefix sum represents 'nothing taken yet'?

known_bugs.name: sliding window that counts one subarray per right end
known_bugs.followup: With zeros in the array, how many different left ends can share the same right end and the same sum?

known_bugs.name: counts subarrays with sum at most goal
known_bugs.followup: Does 'at most goal' equal 'exactly goal'? What would you subtract to isolate exactly goal?

followups: How does the 'at most(goal) - at most(goal-1)' sliding window solution compare?
Why does the zeros case trip up a plain sliding window?
